I have farmed this 3.5 mu in Quzhou for thirty years. My husband and I handle the fields while our children work in the city and send money home. Because of their help, I can buy good inputs, but I am not foolish with money—I do what I know works.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. Now it is waking up from winter sleep. I will topdress urea when it greens up, and again at jointing stage. I will irrigate three times from my well: greening, jointing, and grain filling. I do not trust the sky alone. I will spray twice—once for weeds and once for insects or rust if they come. I use improved wheat seeds because they fight disease better than the old saved seeds. I rotary-tilled before planting last autumn. If the weather is fair, I expect about 1000 jin per mu.

For the summer maize: the same day we cut wheat in early June, we plant maize. There is no time to waste between harvest and planting. I use the no-till seeder to plant hybrid maize directly into the wheat stubble—this saves time and keeps the soil moist. I put compound fertilizer in the hole at planting, and topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage. Two irrigations from the well should be enough if summer rain comes. Two sprays: one for weeds after emergence, one for armyworms if I see them. I expect around 1200 jin per mu.

This is my plan because it has fed six mouths for three decades and leaves some grain to sell. I do not chase every new idea I hear—I follow what my eyes and my mother-in-law taught me.
